stage1.impression: A warm, convincingly laid-out deep bar seen through a window. It still reads as a soft, denoised CG render: smeared record spines, smooth plastic-looking table tops, and a giant flat salmon 'RF' that looks pasted on top rather than etched into glass. The red pair at the far end is tiny and under-lit, the shopfront itself (steel, glass, lightbox) barely appears, and no glass reflections tell you there is a pane. As it stands a magazine would read it as a generic warehouse bar, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The shopfront must be the subject: the blackened-steel frame, the glass as a visible pane (street reflections, a faint sheen), the etched name and the frosted dancer lightbox all in frame. Right now only one mullion and two letters show.
The etched name must read as acid-etched glass (translucent, lit from the room behind and a little from the street), not as an opaque flat panel at lum 173 that tops the frame.
The Ember pair must be the obvious hero at a glance: brighter (region lum_median >= 60) and large enough to read as horn speakers rather than two red boxes.
At the delivered 2400 px there must be no denoiser smear on the record spines and bottles, and the table tops need a real material response.
One sign that this place is specific (the altar, the Domes, the lightbox), so it can't be mistaken for a generic exposed-beam bar.

defects.what: Etched name reads as an opaque, flat, pale-pink painted panel (lum_median 173, uniform). No frosting, no glass, no light falloff, and only 'RF' is in frame.
A single steel mullion splits the frame at about 30 % width, the only shopfront element visible. It reads as a column in the room, not as a shopfront.
No glass reflection anywhere (street lamps, kerb, the camera side), so the pane is invisible and the 'from the kerb' premise is lost.
Left Ember: lum_median 46.6, about 35 px wide. It reads as a small red box with a grey disc, not as a tinted cast-acrylic horn speaker.
Right Ember: lum_median 39.2, below the 45 target and dimmer than the left one.
Record wall spines are denoiser-smeared into colour bands with no sleeve edges or text.
The framed screen or print on the right wall is the brightest surface in the room (lum_median 118) and pulls the eye away from the altar.
The foreground table top is smooth, uniform and plastic-looking, with a cut-off Orb lamp at the edge.
A Dome pendant reads as a bare white blown disc rather than a tinted acrylic lamp.
The concrete floor reflection is plausible but smeared, with no aggregate or saw-cut detail.

changes.problem: The frame is meant to show the shopfront at night, but the camera is 1.6 m from the glass and sees straight through it, so the facade, the lightbox and most of the name are out of frame.

evidence.measured: The only shopfront elements are one mullion (x 200-235, lum_median 15) and the letters 'RF' (x 0-150). No lightbox, no sill, no frame head, no pavement.

change.from: position [-1.6, 2.9, 1.45], lens 40 mm, f/5.6 focused at [0.0, 3.0, 1.6]
change.to: position [-5.0, 2.4, 1.5] (across the pavement, slightly off-axis toward the right-hand wall), aimed at [17.0, 3.2, 1.4], lens 35 mm, f/8 focused at [0.0, 3.0, 1.6], verticals kept level (shift instead of tilt if the head of the frame is cut)

changes.expected: The full steel shopfront, the whole etched name and the frosted dancer lightbox frame the room. The deep interior and the altar sit in the glass as a picture within a picture, with pavement in the lower tenth.

changes.problem: The etched name looks like opaque painted vinyl, flat and brighter than anything in the room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 173.4, p5-p95 9.5-176.4 (a flat plateau), RGB 197/168/157, no gradient.

change.setting: the window's etched name (emission strength), and frosted acrylic/glass roughness
change.to: emission 0.05; make it a rough transmissive etch (roughness about 0.6, transmission on) so the room shows through it as a blur and it catches the street lamps on its edges

changes.expected: The letters read as satin-frosted glass, a little lighter than what is behind them and with visible variation. They are no longer the brightest object in the frame.

changes.problem: The Ember pair, the hero, is too dim and too small to read as speakers from the kerb.

evidence.measured: Right Ember lum_median 39.2, left 46.6 (target 45 or more). The red is about 35 px wide at proof scale.

change.setting: the altar spots; the area lamps on each Ember speaker
change.from: altar 2 x 90 W, 36 deg; Ember area 1.0 W/m2
change.to: altar 2 x 170 W, 30 deg; Ember area 2.2 W/m2, balanced so both speakers match

changes.expected: The red acrylic glows through and the horn mouth and white batts read. The pair becomes the brightest coloured thing in the room, both speakers within 5 lum of each other.

changes.problem: There is no evidence of a glass pane or a street, so this doesn't read as a photograph from the kerb.

evidence.measured: No specular reflections on the glass plane. The street lamps (3 x 90 W, 3000 K) leave no visible trace.

change.to: 3 x point, 140 W, 3200 K, one placed behind and to the left of the camera so its reflection and a faint mirrored kerb and parked-car shape lie in the lower-left glass, plus a sodium-warm wash on the pavement and the steel sill

changes.expected: A faint, clean reflection layer across 10-20 % of the glass, the pavement lit, and the steel frame edges catching a highlight, so the pane becomes real.

changes.problem: The framed screen on the right wall is the brightest surface in the room and competes with the altar.
changes.expected: The screen sits back as a soft glowing panel at about lum 65-80, and the eye goes to the altar.

changes.problem: The denoiser smears fine detail (record spines, bottles, concrete) into CG paste.

evidence.measured: Visual at 3x: the spines are colour bands with no sleeve edges, and the bottles blur into blobs.

change.to: samples 640, adaptive 0.008, denoise on with albedo+normal passes (prefilter accurate), and judge at full 2400 x 1600 rather than at scale 0.3

changes.expected: Spine edges, sleeve text blocks and bottle highlights hold at 1:1, the concrete gets grain, and nothing looks painted.

changes.problem: The Dome pendant in the middle reads as a bare blown white disc rather than tinted acrylic.

evidence.measured: A small white disc at the top of the frame's range (top-band p95 174, clip 0.21 % in [0, 0, 720, 120]).

change.to: 0.6, keeping the 260 W downlights so the pools on the counter stay

changes.expected: The Domes show their tint and the liner as a soft gradient, with no clipping in the ceiling band.

changes.problem: The table tops and the floor are smooth and uniform, a CG giveaway.

evidence.measured: Visual: a uniform tan top with no grain or wear. The floor reflection in [240, 320, 560, 480] is smooth with no aggregate.

change.setting: the materials' finish (the floor's polish, the oak's stain)
change.to: the floor at roughness 0.25-0.4 driven by a large-scale blotch map with saw-cut joints; the table tops with an oak grain bump and ring-mark roughness variation

changes.expected: Softer, broken floor reflections and table tops that read as worn timber at 1:1.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember speakers physically larger or bring the altar forward so the hero reads from the street.
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' size and the room's layout are fixed. Only the camera and the light can make them read.

out_of_scope.request: Drop the second saturated colour (the bottle-green zone and banquette near the altar), which competes with the red.
out_of_scope.why: The zone and its colour are fixed by the room's design.

out_of_scope.request: Add a person at the counter or in the doorway for scale and life.
out_of_scope.why: People aren't among the listed small props; this needs the owner's approval.
